Left-wing populism focuses on economic fairness, while right-wing populism often emphasizes nationalism and stricter immigration policies. On the other hand, leaders like Jair Bolsonaro in Brazil push right-wing populism by focusing on nationalism and strong security measures. Populist leaders often blame economic problems on globalization, big corporations, or government corruption. Leaders like Donald Trump have used populist ideas, such as “America First,” to appeal to voters who feel left behind by the government.
